description: Turning messy real-world data into reliable analysis-ready tables: data sources and file formats, loading with pandas and SQL, cleaning missing and inconsistent values, reshaping, joining and aggregating, handling dates, text and categories, data quality validation and reproducible pipelines. Students wrangle genuinely messy local datasets in a Python and SQL notebook that runs in the browser, and every cleaning step is checked by automated assertions on the resulting data.
modelledOn: Wickham, Cetinkaya-Rundel and Grolemund, R for Data Science (data transformation and tidying chapters)
DAMA International, DAMA-DMBOK: Data Management Body of Knowledge
outcomes: Acquire data from files, databases and APIs and load it correctly, handling formats, encodings and types.
Diagnose and treat missing, duplicated, inconsistent and outlying values, and justify each choice.
Reshape, join and aggregate tables with pandas and SQL while checking keys and cardinality.
Parse and transform dates, free text and categorical variables, including local names and phone numbers.
Define and automate data quality checks and validation rules.
Build reproducible, documented and privacy-aware data preparation pipelines.

units.title: Data sources and file formats
topics: The data life cycle and where wrangling fits; tidy data principles
Delimited text: CSV and TSV, quoting, headers, and character encodings such as UTF-8 and Latin-1
JSON, XML, spreadsheets and columnar formats such as Parquet
Web APIs: authentication, pagination and rate limits; scraping responsibly
Open data portals and exports from DHIS2 district health information systems
Licensing, provenance and documenting where data came from

units.title: Loading data with pandas and SQL
topics: pandas Series and DataFrames; dtypes and the index
read_csv and related readers: parsing options, dtypes, chunking and large files on modest laptops
Selecting and filtering: loc, iloc, boolean masks and query
SQL for wrangling: SELECT, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY and window functions in SQLite
Moving data between SQL databases and pandas
Memory use, vectorisation and avoiding row-by-row loops

units.title: Cleaning missing and inconsistent values
topics: Missingness mechanisms: MCAR, MAR and MNAR; sentinel values and hidden missingness
Deletion versus imputation: mean, median, mode, forward-fill, group-wise and model-based imputation
Inconsistent spellings of district and town names; standardising units and codes
Exact and fuzzy duplicate detection; record linkage
Outliers: detection with IQR, z-scores and domain rules, and deciding what to do
Type coercion and fixing numbers stored as text

units.title: Reshaping, joining and aggregating
topics: Wide and long formats: melt, pivot, pivot_table, stack and unstack
Joins: inner, left, right and outer; join keys, one-to-many and many-to-many cardinality checks
Anti-joins and semi-joins for finding unmatched records
Split-apply-combine with groupby: aggregate, transform and filter
Rolling, expanding and cumulative calculations
Linking cocoa purchase records to a farmer registry and summarising by society and season

units.title: Working with dates, text and categories
topics: Parsing dates in mixed formats; time zones; periods, resampling and fiscal calendars
String methods and regular expressions for extraction and cleaning
Normalising Ghanaian phone numbers to +233 format and validating network prefixes
Unicode normalisation and names in local languages
Categorical data: ordered categories, recoding, binning and one-hot encoding
Geographic data in brief: region and district codes and boundary changes

units.title: Data quality checks and validation
topics: Data quality dimensions: completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, validity and uniqueness
Profiling a dataset; summary statistics as checks
Schema and rule-based validation with assertions and validation libraries
Data dictionaries, data contracts and reporting quality issues to data owners

units.title: Reproducible data pipelines
topics: From notebooks to scripts and functions; method chaining for readable transformations
Version control for code and data; pinned environments
Pipeline orchestration with Make or a lightweight workflow tool; idempotent, restartable steps
Logging and testing transformations
Incremental loads and handling interrupted runs on unreliable power and connectivity

units.title: Privacy, ethics and the capstone
topics: Personal data in datasets: anonymisation, pseudonymisation and re-identification risk
Ghana's Data Protection Act and consent for secondary use of data
Documenting a prepared dataset with a datasheet
Capstone: an end-to-end, validated pipeline from raw public data to an analysis-ready table

schedule.title: Data life cycle and file formats
schedule.exercise: Describe the life cycle of a clinic attendance dataset from collection to analysis and list where wrangling steps occur, with the tidy-data violations you expect.

tasks.title: Identify the three tidy-data violations in a given wide table of weekly cases and rewrite it in tidy form with pandas
Load a CSV with quoted commas, a Latin-1 encoding and a missing header row by choosing the right read options, and verify row and column counts
Read the same records from CSV, JSON and a spreadsheet export, compare dtypes and file sizes, and explain why a columnar format suits large data

schedule.title: Data sources, APIs and provenance
schedule.exercise: Write a short data provenance note for a DHIS2 export covering source, date, licence, known gaps and the steps to reproduce the download.

tasks.title: Parse a DHIS2-style export with period, organisation unit and value columns and reshape it to one row per district per month
Write a loop that pages through a mock API of 120 records, respects a rate limit of 10 calls per minute and stops when the data runs out
Merge two open datasets with different licences, record the provenance of each column in a metadata table and flag which columns cannot be redistributed

schedule.title: pandas fundamentals
schedule.exercise: Answer ten short questions about a market prices DataFrame using selection, filtering and descriptive methods, and explain each choice of loc or iloc.

tasks.title: Create a DataFrame from a dictionary of market prices, inspect dtypes and set a meaningful index
Read a 200000-row file in chunks with chosen dtypes, count rows per region, and compare memory use with a default read
Answer eight questions about a school dataset using loc, iloc, boolean masks and query, including a combined condition on two columns

schedule.title: SQL and efficient wrangling
schedule.exercise: Rewrite a slow row-by-row Python loop as a vectorised or SQL solution and explain why it is faster.

tasks.title: Write SQL to select, filter, join and group a farmer and purchases table in SQLite, returning total purchases per village
Use a window function to rank farmers by purchase value within each society and compute a running total per season
Replace a row-by-row loop over 100000 records with vectorised pandas and compare run time and memory, and move the join into SQL to compare again

schedule.title: Missing and inconsistent values
schedule.exercise: Choose, with reasons, a treatment (delete, impute or flag) for each of five missing-data situations in a health survey.

tasks.title: Find sentinel values such as -999 and N/A hidden in a dataset, convert them to proper missing values and report the count per column
Impute missing yields by mean, median and group-wise median, compare resulting distributions and justify the choice for skewed data
Standardise 40 inconsistent spellings of district names to an official list with a mapping table and verify no unmatched values remain

schedule.title: Duplicates, outliers and types
schedule.exercise: Write a decision note on whether to delete, cap or keep each flagged outlier in a cocoa price dataset, with domain reasoning.

tasks.title: Detect exact duplicate rows and remove them, keeping the most recent, in a registry of 500 records
Flag outliers in farm size using IQR and z-scores, compare the lists and apply a domain rule that farms above 100 hectares need review
Link two beneficiary lists with misspelt names using fuzzy matching, set a similarity threshold and report precision against a given answer key

schedule.title: Reshaping and joining
schedule.exercise: Draw the join diagram for three tables (farmers, farms, purchases), stating the key and cardinality of each join and the expected row counts.

tasks.title: Convert a wide table of monthly rainfall to long form with melt and back to wide with pivot, checking that no values are lost
Join farmers to purchases with inner, left and outer joins, compare row counts and detect a many-to-many blow-up caused by duplicate keys
Use an anti-join in SQL and pandas to find farmers in the registry with no purchases and purchases with no registered farmer

schedule.title: Grouping and window calculations
schedule.exercise: Write a summary of purchases by society and season for a cocoa cooperative, with one paragraph on what you would check before trusting it.

tasks.title: Group sales by region and compute count, sum and mean with agg, then add a column showing each row as a share of its region total using transform
Calculate a 3-month rolling average and a cumulative total of rainfall by station, handling the first rows correctly
Link purchase records to a farmer registry with imperfect IDs, resolve unmatched records and summarise tonnes bought per society per season

schedule.title: Dates, text and phone numbers
schedule.exercise: Write ten regular expressions with test strings for typical cleaning tasks such as phone numbers, receipt codes and district names.

tasks.title: Parse dates in five mixed formats into one standard type, flag the ambiguous ones and resample the series to monthly totals
Extract the receipt number, amount and date from 30 free-text mobile money messages using regular expressions and check against the answer key
Normalise 100 Ghanaian phone numbers with varied spacing and prefixes to +233 form and validate network prefixes, listing the unfixable ones

schedule.title: Unicode, categories and geography
schedule.exercise: Explain with examples how inconsistent Unicode or changing district codes can silently break a join.

tasks.title: Normalise names containing local-language characters to a single Unicode form so that joins match, and show the match count before and after
Bin ages into ordered categories, recode a 5-level satisfaction scale, and one-hot encode region for a modelling table
Map old to new district codes after boundary changes with a crosswalk table, and aggregate historic counts to the new districts without double counting

schedule.title: Data quality and validation
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page data dictionary and quality report for a prepared dataset, with agreed fixes for each issue.

tasks.title: Profile a dataset by computing missing percentage, unique counts and ranges per column, and list five suspicious findings
Write SQL checks for completeness, uniqueness and validity on a patient table and return the failing rows for each rule
Write an assertion-based validation function covering types, ranges, allowed values and referential integrity, and run it on a dataset with seven seeded faults

schedule.title: Reproducible pipelines
schedule.exercise: Refactor a notebook into a script with named functions, and explain how you would run it again after a failure without duplicates.

tasks.title: Rewrite a messy notebook as a chain of small functions using method chaining, and confirm the output equals the original
Create a requirements file with pinned versions and a script that runs the whole cleaning workflow from raw file to clean file
Make a three-step pipeline idempotent so that rerunning it after a failure at step two produces the same final table with no duplicate rows

schedule.title: Privacy, ethics and capstone
schedule.exercise: Write a datasheet for the capstone dataset covering purpose, collection, cleaning steps, known limitations and permitted uses under Ghanaian data protection law.

tasks.title: Pseudonymise a patient table by hashing IDs, generalise age and location, and test with a given attack for the number of unique people remaining
Add logging and three unit tests to a cleaning function, including a test for a seeded bug, and confirm all tests pass after the fix
Build an end-to-end pipeline from a raw public dataset to an analysis-ready table with validation checks, logging and a final data quality report
